fieldDefinition.description: The canonical closed FieldDefinition shape — what to $ref when a field is used as-is. unevaluatedProperties rather than additionalProperties because only the former sees an allOf branch beside it, which is what lets a use site extend the shape (connector configuration fields add `secret`) without the closure rejecting the addition.

fieldDefinitionProperties.description: The canonical FieldDefinition property set, left OPEN so a use site can extend it. Extend this one only alongside your own unevaluatedProperties: false — on its own it closes nothing.

suggestions.description: Where the variable suggestions offered for this field come from. Mirrored onto the generated page field so the renderer can offer the right list; pairs with `variables`.

sourceField.description: Key of a sibling field whose value determines the available suggestions.

sourceKey.description: Fixed suggestion-source key, when the list does not depend on a sibling field.

readOnly.description: Presentation only: render the field with its display component instead of its input component. Not an API contract — use `immutable` for that.

immutable.description: API contract: the field may be set when the record is created and is refused by every generated transport afterwards (REST 400; absent from the GraphQL update input and the MCP update schema). Use it for provenance links and other values that must not be re-pointed once written.

writtenBy.description: API contract: operation contract keys (e.g. `pentest.finding.review`) that are the only writers of this field. The field is absent from the generated create AND update schemas on every transport, and a caller sending it anyway is refused with a message naming these operations. Use it for fields that record that a process took place — a review signed off, a scope approved, a retest concluded — where the operation is the only place the preconditions are checked. Not to be confused with `readOnly`, which selects a display component and enforces nothing. A key no compiled operation answers to fails the build.
